advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] After the best-effort mount in both harnesses, check that the tracker dir exists. If it does not, stop with a clear error, or at least print a warning to stderr and record it in the results, before running any model.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_init.py:180: except (Exception, SystemExit) as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — best-effort: never propagate to CLI
src/rebar/_cli/_init.py:168-169: if not root: return  (silent no-op)
src/rebar/llm/evals/provider_parity.py:640: _mount_existing_store()  — result not checked; line 641 goes straight to LLMConfig.from_env() and run_slot
src/rebar/llm/evals/engine_comparison.py:473: ensure_store_mounted_best_effort()  — result not checked before run()
Absence: neither harness checks config.tracker_dir(root).is_dir() (or anything similar) after the mount call, so 'mounted' and 'mount silently failed' produce the same result.
advisory.finding: Both harnesses call ensure_store_mounted_best_effort() but never check that a store is mounted afterwards. The helper swallows every failure, so a run can still go ahead against an unattached store. Every show_ticket read then fails with 'ticket system not initialized' (provider_parity), or titles silently fall back to prose (engine_comparison), and the run gives no sign of it. This is the same unattributable-verdict bug the commit sets out to fix.
scenarios: A linked worktree where init_core returns nonzero or raises: the mount is skipped with only a debug log, and the parity run then scores every agentic case as a runtime error on both arms.
REBAR_ROOT or git resolution returns no root, or the store is neither a symlink nor an attachable existing branch: the call does nothing and engine_comparison silently uses prose titles.
advisory.suggested_fix: After calling ensure_store_mounted_best_effort(), check the result. If config.tracker_dir_override() is unset and config.repo_root_or_none() gives a root, but config.tracker_dir(root).is_dir() is still False, write an error to stderr and return 2 before any run_slot/run call. Put this in one shared helper so both harnesses use it.
